text: The time should likewise be judiciously chosen; every man has his 'mollia tempora', but that is far from being all day long; and you would choose your time very ill, if you applied to a man about one business, when his head was full of another, or when his heart was full of grief, anger, or any other disagreeable sentiment.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXI, to his son, London, May 22, Old Style 1749
